title: About the centre of its circle the planet moves unequally: the arc DE is less than the arc EF, and both are passed in equal times
author: Gerd Graßhoff

context.title: The equant model of the first inequality

model.title: The equant model of the first inequality

parameters.name: R
parameters.meaning: radius of the eccentric circle about B

parameters.name: e
parameters.meaning: eccentricity BA: the distance of the eye from the centre

parameters.name: q
parameters.meaning: the distance BC of the equant point from the centre

parameters.name: T
parameters.meaning: period of the planet about the equant point

parameters.name: theta_0
parameters.meaning: the angle at the equant point at t = 0

variables.name: theta
variables.meaning: the angle DCE at the equant point, counted from the apogee

objects.name: orb
objects.meaning: the eccentric, the circle the planet traverses

objects.name: E
objects.meaning: the planet: where the line from C at the angle θ meets the circle

observables.name: lam
observables.meaning: longitude of the planet as seen from A

observables.name: atC
observables.meaning: the angle DCE at the equant point

observables.name: atB
observables.meaning: the angle DBE at the centre: the arc DE the planet has traversed

hypotheses.claim: the equant point lies as far above the centre as the eye lies below it: BC = BA

argument.claim: the angle DBE at the centre is less than the angle DCE at the equant point
argument.formal: less(angle(D, B, E), angle(D, C, E))

children.claim: DCE is the exterior angle of the triangle CBE, equal to the interior angles CBE and CEB
children.formal: equal(angle(E, C, D), angle(C, E, B) + angle(E, B, C))

by.statement: In any triangle, if one of the sides be produced, the exterior angle is equal to the two interior and opposite angles, and the three interior angles of the triangle are equal to two right angles.

children.note: configuration conditions fail there: noncollinear(E, B, C)
conditions: B, C, D on one line

children.claim: the part CEB taken away, the remainder CBE is less than DCE
children.formal: less(angle(E, B, C), angle(E, C, D))

by.statement: The whole is greater than the part.

children.claim: CBE or DBE: C and D lie from B on one ray
children.formal: equal(angle(E, B, C), angle(D, B, E))

by.statement: The proposition is read off the cited constructions: it holds for every parameter value and every state without any hypothesis.

children.formal: less(angle(D, B, E), angle(D, C, E))

by.statement: Things which are equal to the same thing are also equal to one another.

argument.claim: BE stands on the apsidal line at B: DBE and EBF make two right angles
argument.formal: equal(angle(D, B, E) + angle(E, B, F), 180°)

by.statement: If a straight line set up on a straight line make angles, it will make either two right angles or angles equal to two right angles.

conditions: D, B, F on one line

argument.claim: CE stands on the apsidal line at C: DCE and ECF make two right angles
argument.formal: equal(angle(D, C, E) + angle(E, C, F), 180°)

by.statement: If a straight line set up on a straight line make angles, it will make either two right angles or angles equal to two right angles.

conditions: D, C, F on one line

argument.claim: so the angle FBE is greater than the angle FCE
argument.formal: less(angle(E, C, F), angle(E, B, F))

children.formal: less(angle(E, C, F), angle(E, B, F))

by.statement: The proposition follows from the cited equalities by calculation.

argument.claim: let DCE be a right angle, and so ECF: two quarters of the period
the arc DE, which measures the angle DBE, is less than the arc EF, which measures the angle EBF
argument.formal: less(angle(D, B, E), angle(E, B, F))

children.claim: the angles at C are equal: they are made in equal times
children.formal: equal(angle(D, C, E), angle(E, C, F))

by.statement: The proposition follows from the cited equalities by calculation.

children.formal: less(angle(D, B, E), angle(E, B, F))

by.statement: The proposition follows from the cited equalities by calculation.

conclusion.claim: in equal times the planet passes the lesser arc DE and the greater arc EF: the orb is now slow, now fast
conclusion.formal: less(angle(D, B, E), angle(E, B, F))

notes: given h1 (equal(q, e)) is not needed for the conclusion

degenerate states, in which a step's rule does not apply, a term is undefined or an inequality becomes an equality: theta = 0°; theta = 180°. The derivation does not cover them; the conclusion is true there as well (numerically)
